page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.12xlarge is an instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family, operating under the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs at a base clock frequency of 3.4 GHz. This hardware configuration is built specifically to address computational requirements where single-thread clock velocity and high parallel execution density are essential.

Memory allocation is structured at 96.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a compute-optimized 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. Dedicated local storage is not bundled, which requires the operational environment to attach remote block storage for the operating system and user data. Accelerators such as GPUs are absent from this configuration.

Resource density on this server maximizes processor efficiency by omitting surplus memory overhead, resulting in favorable resource economics for CPU-bound pipelines. Primary architectural tradeoffs involve dependence on networked storage for storage I/O and strict memory limits per vCPU. Best-fit use cases include software compilation pipelines, automated CI/CD runners, scientific batch computing, media processing, and high-throughput application servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.12xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented instance from the High Clock Speed family built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at 3.4 GHz, the server delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 96.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity operates at a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps, while GPU hardware acceleration and integrated local storage are omitted. With persistent storage requiring network-attached block devices, system resource allocation directly prioritizes processing throughput over local data caching or large memory tables. This configuration delivers an efficient profile for environments that maximize multi-threaded CPU cycles without incurring unnecessary memory overhead. Primary suitable workloads include code compilation clusters, compute-heavy microservices, media transcoding, scientific simulations, and continuous integration engines.
